response: Yes, covering the resection margin after distal pancreatectomy can be advantageous. This technique, often involving the use of a falciform ligament, omental flap, or other tissue, may help reduce the risk of pancreatic fistula, a common complication following distal pancreatectomy. By covering the resection margin, it is possible to minimize exposure of the pancreatic stump to the surrounding tissue and decrease the likelihood of enzymatic leakage, thereby potentially lowering the incidence of postoperative pancreatic fistula and other related complications.
